target.name: PreyVR optional zero-g fixed-surface grab and scoped push-off

question: Can fixed-surface anchoring and physical push-off use a proved native zero-g movement seam with no teleport, scoped restoration and no launch from invalidation, according to static and offline evidence?
claim: Steam instructions and concrete tables establish the primary animated AddMovement receiver, exact zero-g type4 caller/request prefix, synchronous velocity copy and native movement time conversion/action path. The implementation changes only 12 request velocity bytes for that current-player caller, restoring them after one native consumer invocation. Pure and actual production-adapter fixtures confirm deliberate grip acquisition, tracking-space motion rather than world differencing, bounded outward/tangential release, context/ownership cancellation and one-use acknowledged release delivery. The actual production transaction restores poisoned request bytes on normal return and SEH. This confirms static/source and synthetic harness contracts, not native gameplay acceptance.
method: MSVC 19.50 x64 Release, Visual Studio 18 2026, CMake/CTest and Python 3.12 read-only PE verification. EGS/PDB exports supplied names and masked-prefix navigation leads; actual Steam instructions, concrete tables and numerical constants establish the target contract. Ghidra preflight found a System Shock 2 session and left it alone. verify_surface_grab.py checks complete Steam identity, native witnesses and runtime FNV gates, with corrupt concrete-callee/request-type/collider-word/hash controls. Pure numerical cases and actual production SurfaceGrabLane.cpp boundary-substitution fixture cover ownership and one-shot leases; actual InvokeMovement runs against a poisoned request under normal and injected SEH paths. Final build and 85/85 offline tests pass. Production Flight-page raster inspected. Reproduction commands are in docs/evidence/surface-grab-2026-10-26/README.md. Code graph refreshed with three explicitly reported partial-parse warnings; no semantic corpus or fleet graph rebuild. No game, injection, XR session, runtime change or headset test.

identity.reason: Full supported Steam module SHA256, x64 PE conventions, source commit and tested DLL identity pinned.

instrument.reason: Independent native instruction/table/constants and runtime-gate correspondence verified with reached corruption controls; fixtures execute actual adapter and transaction with named native/publication/query substitutions; production GDI painter checked.

control.reason: Valid fixed contact versus miss/backface/movable/removed contact; raw physical hand motion versus body/camera drift; exact native caller/entity/type versus unrelated requests; fresh versus expired leases, re-grip and changed reference/menu/player/weapon/settings; native cleanup and use/equipment priority; normal versus injected SEH restoration.

scene.reason: Static files and synthetic offline fixtures only, not an ordinary zero-g game scene.

restore.reason: Persistent version-controlled source work. Transaction restoration was separately measured in the fixture. No target process, user settings, runtime registration or existing package was changed.

baseline.reason: Release build, native static verifier/corruption controls and 85/85 combined offline tests pass. This is source/harness health only, not launch, actual physics, surface coverage or headset acceptance.

limits: No hook execution against Prey, native collision/flight acceptance, exhaustive fixed-surface coverage, save transitions, headset comfort or performance measurement. Single free left-hand anchor only; props/living bodies and moving-support following/bimanual anchoring excluded. A constructor-zeroed collider word is an additional conservative gate; its semantic name is not relied upon. Held anchors re-probe locally with tolerances; this is not exhaustive detection of sub-tolerance script movement. Existing inertia can remain after cancellation. Native consumer return proves submission, not that subsequent physics applied the requested motion. Optional development source/build, not a release or headset-approved artifact.
